decisions.executionNote: Approach the charger in the right workspace, beginning an elbow-up downward-facing grasp orientation; left arm stays home.
Raise and tip the right wrist over the charger, retaining elbow-up continuity and observing its axis before descent.
Continue the right-arm pregrasp approach, aligning the open jaws to the charger's long axis.
Lower toward the charger with open fingers; use the right wrist image to refine lateral and yaw alignment before closing.
Fine-align the charger's body between the jaws while descending slowly; keep the gripper open until the body is centered.
Correct the wrist-image offset and yaw before grasping; the charger is not yet centered, so keep the jaws open.
Refine the grasp using the charger silhouette: small sideways and backward correction to center it between the open fingers.
Use a small opposite lateral correction to center the charger in the wrist view before closing.
Translate without rotation to resolve the wrist-view lateral offset; maintain grasp height and open jaws.
Make a short forward centering adjustment at fixed wrist orientation; inspect the body position before closing.
Center the body from the measured wrist-image response, then close the right gripper to grasp it.
Finish closing, then lift a short distance while checking visually that the charger remains between the jaws.
The charger appears retained. Lift clear of the table before changing its grasp orientation for upright insertion.
Move the held charger toward a central handoff pose; a regrasp is needed so the prongs can point down without putting the wrist below the tabletop.
Continue rotating the retained charger for handoff while bringing the left arm forward in its own workspace, with open jaws.
Advance both wrists toward a separated central handoff arrangement, retaining the charger in the right gripper.
Bring the left gripper toward the exposed charger end while the right finishes its handoff orientation; keep the wrists on their respective sides.
Finish presenting the charger horizontally at the center while advancing the open left gripper from the left.
Align the open left gripper with the exposed charger end for a supported regrasp, keeping the right hand stationary.
Complete the left pregrasp alignment at the exposed end; the right gripper continues supporting the charger.
Advance the open left fingers around the free end of the charger, keeping the right grip closed until the handoff is secured.
Close the remaining approach gap at the charger end with small translations, keeping both wrists separated and the left jaws open.
Close the left gripper around the exposed charger end while the right continues supporting it; verify the handoff before releasing.
Release the right grip after the left closes, then withdraw slightly. Reorient the right hand for an end-on grasp that permits upright insertion in its workspace.
Clear the right fingers from the charger while the left supports it, creating space to turn it upright for a second handoff.
Keep the charger supported on the left and approach the strip's right end with the open right hand, to relocate the socket toward a shared central insertion area without crossing arms.
Align the right jaws across the strip's far-right end while keeping the charger lifted safely in the left hand.
Continue the right-hand top-down approach over the strip end; the left holds the charger steady above the table.
Finish orienting the right gripper vertically over the strip end, then reassess its grasp height from the wrist image.
Lower the right fingers toward the strip's end section for a side pinch, making a small centering correction.
Position the right pads around the solid end section of the power strip, descending slowly before closing.
Close the right gripper around the strip end while the left continues holding the charger; verify retention before moving the strip.
Lift the strip slightly to confirm the end grasp, keeping both objects clear before repositioning the socket toward the center.
The strip remains between the right pads. Carry it toward the center and turn its socket row for a left-side insertion, keeping the wrists on their own sides.
Turn the strip level across the center while lifting and beginning to orient the charger upright; preserve clearance between both held objects.
Carry the strip farther toward the center; raise and rotate the retained charger to prepare prongs-down alignment.
Bring the strip to a central supported location while gradually turning the charger prongs downward above the left-side sockets.
Lower the held strip toward the table at center and continue the charger's upright rotation with clearance above it.
Release the strip onto the tabletop and withdraw the right fingers, while continuing to orient the charger above the empty left-side socket.
Clear the right wrist away from the placed strip, and continue rotating the left-held charger toward prongs-down alignment.
Finish the charger's upright orientation above the strip's left socket and move the right hand clear.
Align the upright charger over the leftmost socket, correcting the lateral offset while lowering to a safe pre-insertion height.
Make a small horizontal correction above the first socket and descend gradually, keeping the left wrist on its side of center.
Center the charger over the visible two-prong slot pair and descend slowly toward engagement, maintaining its upright orientation.
Advance the upright charger vertically into the aligned socket in small increments, watching for seating rather than relying on tracking alone.
Attempt the final few millimeters of vertical seating gently; the charger appears upright, but full insertion is not yet visually confirmed.
Release the upright charger at its seated position, then begin clearing the fingers to inspect whether it remains fully engaged.
Lift the open left fingers clear to inspect the charger's independent seating, and begin retracting the right arm toward home.
The charger remains upright without the fingers. Retract both open hands toward their home workspaces while maintaining elbow-up continuity.
The exposed prongs show insertion is incomplete. Return the open left fingers to regrasp and correct the small front-back socket offset.
The charger has tipped behind the strip rather than seating. Approach it from the rear with open fingers so a new grasp can orient the prongs downward without a low wrist.
Pause after the continuity guard and close at the current aligned body location to check a secure regrasp before any further translation.
The body is behind the fingers rather than retained. Reopen and move toward it with small fixed-orientation steps, lowering to avoid the previous continuity limit.
Approach the fallen charger's body with open jaws, tilting slightly toward it while moving the left wrist away from its reach limit.
Lower the open left jaws around the charger body, using the wrist image for a small centering correction before regrasping.
Center the fallen charger's body between the left pads and close for a controlled regrasp; the previous insertion was not complete.
Lift the regrasped charger a short distance and check visually that it follows the left gripper before reorienting it.
The charger did not follow the lift. Reopen and lower the pads farther around its body, correcting the small sideways offset.
Lower and center the left pads around the charger's sides, then close without moving the strip.
Ease upward with the left gripper closed to clear contact and check whether the charger follows the pads.
Lift the regrasped charger clear of the strip and retreat slightly, watching for stable retention before correcting its orientation.
The charger now follows the left pads. Lift and retreat to create clearance for rotating its prongs downward before another insertion attempt.
Rotate the retained charger toward prongs-down while retreating the left wrist to preserve object clearance above the table.
Continue turning the securely held charger upright with the wrist behind it, maintaining clearance for a fresh socket alignment.
Continue the upright reorientation at a safe height, shifting left slightly so the charger can be inspected clear of the strip.
Bring the charger toward a vertical prongs-down attitude with the wrist behind it, moving toward the left socket while retaining clearance.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller rotation increments, lowering and retreating the wrist while keeping the charger retained.
Lower the retained charger toward a new upright approach, finishing the rotation slowly while keeping the left wrist behind the socket.
Lower the upright charger toward the left socket, refining yaw and lateral alignment while retaining the body securely.
Descend toward the socket with the charger held upright; reposition the clear right wrist slightly to improve the side view of the prongs.
Approach the socket slowly while improving the right-side inspection view; do not release until prong engagement can be checked.
Correct a small rearward and lateral offset seen relative to the socket, then approach a few millimeters while keeping the charger upright and held.
Use the visible pin and slot pair for another small alignment correction, then lower gently while retaining the charger.
The visible pins now align with the outer socket slots. Attempt a shallow vertical engagement while holding the charger upright.
The side view suggests the prongs remain behind the slot row. Lift slightly and bring the held charger forward before trying engagement again.
With the prongs visually over the outer slot pair, lower five millimeters gradually and check for actual engagement.
The visible prong gap has decreased. Continue a slow four-millimeter seating motion while retaining the upright charger.
Make a millimeter-scale forward alignment correction with a shallow seating motion; the remaining prong gap is small but not yet confirmed closed.
Release at the aligned socket and withdraw the left fingers backward slightly, checking whether the charger settles independently rather than pushing farther under uncertain contact.
The released charger has settled upright with no exposed prong gap. Clear both open hands and begin returning to their home positions.
The charger remains upright on the socket after withdrawal. Continue the separated, open-handed return toward each arm's origin.
Continue returning both open hands, raising the left wrist to preserve elbow-up clearance and configuration continuity.
